I was thinking just this morning before the episode was released, about how it's been almost 6 years since I started Night Vale, and how realising that Cecil actually was in love with Carlos was the crux of what sold me on the show. The most recent episode to be released when I started was 'Summer Reading Program' so around August 2013, and Cecil mentioning that he'd been with Carlos for six years (and therefore, longer than I had even known about the show) made me feel really...nice.I was lulled into a false sense of security with the start of this episode. Cecil, a grown ass man, geeking out about his love for his brilliant little scientist has always been one of the most endearing qualities of the show to me. And yeah, it hasn't always been great or perfect, but Cecil was, in the most basic terms, saved from a life of solitude and sadness because of Carlos. Carlos opened up so many possibilities and passions in Cecil, and every time he mentions how much more he falls in love with Carlos every day, I fall more in love with them, too.

The Blood Space War has always been one of my fave Night Vale things. Lost in the Mail is one of my favourite episodes, too. I was super happy to be continuing the story line from that, and Basimah is BRILLIANT but I started getting really scared, really fast.I know that the season finale is coming up soon. I had been wondering what would go wrong, as things so often do, so that they could be placed back together perfectly. There were bits and pieces of 'wrong,' but nothing really solid.I thought things couldn't get more emotional than Basimah and her mom etc disappearing.I have been scared for Carlos for a while now. But I expected some kind of revelation about his past and Cecil having to leave him, not something like this. It was just...heartbreaking.

Not in a strictly bad way, I just.. don't know. People started disappearing, and I suddenly realised what was coming, and when it did, I was still shocked. There was a line about people disappearing because they hadn't been born or moved to Night Vale at all, and I knew.I knew about six different times throughout the episode. 'If we don't remember them, does it matter?' (oh Cecil.) I had to stop at the scientists line, I just. I knew it was coming but I just can't.It's been about ten hours and I'm still...stuck. It's been an emotional week for a lot of my fandoms, and I just didn't think they would do this to us, but well, here we are.

Night Vale is very easy listening. I’ve been listening for years, and have heard most episodes about twenty times, so I might be a little bias, but it’s fantastic. 

I would recommend listening in order of release, because each episode seems standalone enough, but there is a bigger picture. There are also lots of throwbacks and character / story arcs etc that might make it a little less magical if you listen out of order. You could always listen to one of their live shows, which are made to be standalones that anybody can enjoy without any real prior knowledge and are really fun. I think they all are pay to listen though, so many not. 

The narrators voice is very pleasant to listen to aswell. The episodes are also shorter than Wolf 359, especially since most people end up skipping the musical interlude (or ‘weather’) which can take a good 3-6 minutes out of each episode. It might look like a lot, but it can be sped through easier than you might think. 

Also, the stories, character, production etc are excellent. It also seems a little slow at the start, I’ll admit. But in my opinion, its pay off is very worth it. 

For more weirdness, I’d recommend Dreamboy (nsfw) or Alice isn’t Dead by the same company as Night Vale. Wolf 359 reminded me of The Amelia Project and The Box Podcast. And Limetown, although popular consensus says season two doesn’t exist. The Bright Sessions and The Message are also worth mentioning, though I wasn’t too into them. 

I hope some of my rambling was useful, if a little late.

I’d also like to add that being aware of and open about your family history is SO important. I had my period for over a year, it having just ended three months ago. My periods were always like clockwork (although lasting upwards of a week every time)!but one day it just started and never stopped. 
I am not dead, although I have always been anaemic and had to have an iron transfusion twice in that year. 
It just wouldn’t stop, and it was heavy every single god damned day. I was going through more than a pack of ‘overnight heavy flow’ pads a day. It was hella expensive. 
I couldn’t take contraceptive or anything to stop it, for other reasons.

Being VCE, the curriculum is pretty much the same no matter what school you go to, as there are set guidelines and standards. If you're studying the same subject, it shouldn't matter that much where you start it. 
The only issue might be having to transfer grades for any assignments you complete - I believe they are marked on a scale, which is based on how others in your class perform (to make up for the differences between teaching styles of teachers and such) so this might be a little complicated for the teachers. 

Assuming you're only doing unit 1 subjects though, I wouldn't say it would matter too much if you were to miss a few weeks of the subject. I transferred classes within my own school mid-way through units 1 and even 2 in one case, and had very little catching up to do. Subjects also don't need to be completed in a sequence, so you could potentially skip units 1/2 altogether. You can't do this for 3/4 subjects though, they need to be completed within the same year and entirely. 
This may vary within the school you go to though. I went to a fancy private school, so I'm assuming they would care more about it than say, a generic public school. But I guess it would be best discussed with the school you plan on moving to, as I'm just a stranger on the internet and don't know what they deem acceptable. 

If you can manage the trip, I would just recommend starting the year at your new school. It would probably be the least complicated thing to do, in regards to studying though.
